subject: chemistry
title: Substances in natural water
key_idea: Water from natural sources contains dissolved and suspended substances. Some are beneficial, such as dissolved oxygen. Others are harmful, such as sewage, plastics, and nitrates and phosphates from fertilisers and detergents. Distilled water is used in the lab because it has fewer impurities.

blocks.text: Water from taps and rivers contains dissolved substances. This section covers why labs use distilled water and how to test purity.

items: Tap water contains dissolved chemical impurities, such as metal compounds.
These impurities could react in an experiment and change the results.
**Distilled water** contains far fewer chemical impurities, so it is used in practical chemistry.
A physical test shows whether water is pure: it boils at exactly 100 °C and freezes at exactly 0 °C.
Impure water boils at a higher temperature than 100 °C and freezes at a lower temperature than 0 °C.
Distilled water is used because it has fewer impurities than tap water.
Pure water boils at 100 °C and freezes at 0 °C.

blocks.text: Many substances can be found in water from rivers, lakes and the sea. This section covers what they are and what they do.

rows: Beneficial: aquatic life needs it to respire
Some provide essential minerals. Some are toxic
Harmful: contains microbes that cause disease
Harmful: lead to deoxygenation of water
Harmful: lead to deoxygenation of water

items: Too many nitrates or phosphates cause the water to lose dissolved oxygen.
Fish and other aquatic life then cannot survive.
Details of how this happens (eutrophication) are not required.

diagram.alt: A sorting activity. Eight substances found in water are sorted into beneficial and harmful.
diagram.prompt: Sort each substance into beneficial or harmful.

items.text: Metal compounds that provide essential minerals

items: Dissolved oxygen and some metal compounds are beneficial.
Toxic metal compounds, plastics, sewage, microbes, nitrates and phosphates are harmful.
Nitrates and phosphates lead to deoxygenation.

checks.q: Explain why distilled water is used in practical chemistry rather than tap water.
checks.a: Distilled water contains fewer chemical impurities, which could interfere with the reaction.

checks.q: Give one beneficial substance found in natural water.
checks.a: Dissolved oxygen, which aquatic life needs. Some metal compounds provide essential minerals.

checks.q: State two harmful substances found in natural water.
checks.a: Any two from: some metal compounds, plastics, sewage, harmful microbes, nitrates, phosphates.

worked_example.question: Pure water is obtained from sodium chloride solution by simple distillation. Describe a physical test to show that the liquid collected is pure water.
answer_points: Or: measure its freezing point, which is 0 °C.
worked_example.tip: Give the test and the value you expect.
